original_question: For a phase-retrieval model in which an object is represented as a background plus a finite sum of translated feature measures, how can one choose the number of features N and decide which feature templates mu_j should be included in the parametrized representation?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Question 4.2, in the context of the object-parameterization model (5): "How can one select the number of features N and the features μ_j?"
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core of the paper's official question very well. It correctly identifies the relevant model class: an object represented as a background term plus a finite sum of translated feature measures, and it focuses on the two exact unknowns singled out in Question 4.2, namely the feature count N and the chosen features μ_j. It also stays in the right section of the paper, namely the physics-informed object-parameterization discussion rather than the later sparse-crystallography simplification.
missing_details: The exact target is Section 4.1, Question 4.2, and it is posed for the general measure-valued parametrization in equation (5), not for the later simplified sparse-crystallography model in equations (7), (9), and (10).
The model itself should be stated explicitly: f = a0 λ + Σ_{j=1}^N a_j S_{t_j} μ_j(σ).
The 'background' is specifically the term a0 λ, where λ is the Lebesgue measure representing the general object background.
The μ_j are not arbitrary templates: they are described as normalized, localized, complex-valued measures representing object features.

Each μ_j is assumed to belong to an admissible feature set E, and the paper distinguishes two separate issues: establishing E itself (Question 4.1) versus selecting the actual μ_j used in the representation (Question 4.2).
The operator S_{t_j} is the translation operator centering μ_j at position t_j; the coefficients a_j encode feature strengths; and the feature measures may depend on an experimental parameter σ.

The ambient setting here is a continuous/infinite-dimensional complex-measure model; the finite-dimensional vector model in C^n appears only later as a simplification and is not the target of Question 4.2.

The nearby context adds a concrete suggested route: start from a pixel-wise reconstruction, then transition to a parametrized model, possibly through a coupled model in which the parametrization acts as a prior or regularization term.

There are no homogeneity, degree, nilpotency, or 'for all sufficiently large m' conditions attached to this question; the hidden assumptions that matter are the complex measure model, the admissible-feature framework, and the phase-retrieval setting.
refined_question: In the physics-informed object-parameterization model for phaseless reconstruction, f = a0 λ + Σ_{j=1}^N a_j S_{t_j} μ_j(σ), where λ is the Lebesgue-measure background, each μ_j is a normalized localized complex measure chosen from an admissible feature set E, S_{t_j} translates μ_j to position t_j, a_j gives its strength, and σ captures experimental conditions, how should one determine the number of features N and the specific feature measures μ_j appearing in the parametrized representation from the phase-retrieval problem data?
justification: The draft is closest to Section 4.1, Question 4.2, not to any statement in later sections. The paper first defines the object-parameterization model in equation (5) and explains the roles of λ, E, μ_j, t_j, a_j, and σ on pages 9-10. It then asks exactly, on page 10, 'How can one select the number of features N and the features μ_j?', with the explanatory discussion continuing onto page 11. The sentence after Question 4.2 says that one possible approach is to use a pixel-wise reconstruction to transition to a parametrized model, and further suggests a coupled model in which the parametrized model is used as a prior or regularizer. Your draft is therefore substantively correct, but to be stand-alone and paper-faithful it needs the full equation (5) context, the admissible-feature set E, the meanings of λ, S_{t_j}, a_j, and σ, and the distinction between Question 4.1 (constructing E) and Question 4.2 (selecting N and the actual μ_j).
